speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify your symptoms: does the altered mentation manifest as confusion, lethargy, or disorientation, and have you experienced any seizures or headaches? Additionally, have you noticed any rash or recent insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, did you notice any muscle rigidity, tremors, or changes in your bowel or bladder function recently?

Also, have you had any recent travel to rural areas or outdoor activities where you might have been bitten by a tick or mosquito?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

I am confident in this diagnosis given the classic tetrad of fever, altered mental status, severe generalized rigidity, and profuse diaphoresis while on haloperidol. No further tests are required to confirm this clinical picture.
